goals.title: The sea keeps what fits
goals.critique: This is the seventh version of the sea-builds-land candidate (rounds 3 to 6). It finally settles the trade-off of the last two rounds. Lumi can dig, carry and stamp sand again, and the sea's scour is the reason hand-building loses, so the Minecraft verbs come back without wiping out the indirect one. The far rock now gives a real payoff (pink sand and the clay the kiln needs), and storms that take whatever does not fit the water are a better clock than a sulking Pickles. The weak parts are the ones that have stood for seven rounds. The pitch is a run-on paragraph rather than one plain line. 'Building by hand alone loses' is a claim about tuning that has not been tested. And not a single wave has been filmed beside a stone, so a readable tongue and a scour hole forming within seconds are still promises, not something anyone has seen.

goals.title: Learn to fly in my own body
goals.critique: The crashes are the strong part. Real, unanimated tumbles, wing tips catching branches and friends laughing are exactly the clips people send, and the island as a course of named gaps gives each try a clear result within seconds. But two keys that drive a floppy body which flails at a skill task is a crowded genre of deliberately clumsy physics games, and learning to fly is an old premise, so the novelty rests on Lumi's own body and not on the mechanic. It also stands on two unbuilt hard parts: the simulated body (#623) and a balance controller that has to survive blade-element flight. Nothing is dug, gathered or built, so the island stays a backdrop, and once the player can fly, the reason to keep playing is gone.
